title: Airport boss defends £453m car parking income

input.lead: Manchester Airport Group boss Chris Woodroofe responds to criticism over parking charges
input.summary: Manchester Airport Group boss Chris Woodroofe responds to criticism over parking charges
input.evidence_text: Airport boss defends £453m car parking income - BBC News Image caption, Chris Woodroofe said about a third of Manchester Airports Group income is from parking By Roger Johnson , North West and Lynette Horsburgh , North West Published 16 minutes ago The boss of Manchester Airport has defended car parking charges there, arguing they are "competitive". Chris Woodroofe was responding to a customer who asked how the airport can justify more than £150 charge for parking for two weeks. The managing director said the cost was "exactly the same sort of charge" as parking in a town centre for the day, but some customers have said they felt the chanrges were unreasonable. Manchester Airports Group (MAG) - which also includes London Stansted and East Midlands Airports - recently recorded it had made £453m from parking, about a third of its income. Woodroofe told BBC North West Tonight : "If you go into the town centre and look to park for a day in the town centre and do that comparison with the £150 for two weeks, it's exactly the same sort of charge." He said the airport was competing with Uber and taxi firms as well as other parking firms. "The car parking world is a competitive one. We are not the only suppliers of car parking in this market place. There are several other competitors, and so it operates a competitive market place." Image source, Manchester Airport Image caption, Chris Woodroofe said Manchester Airport's drop off charges was the lowest charge of any of the big airports across the UK However, he said comparing the cost of parking in a town centre for a day "isn't really like-for-like". title: Man stabbed in Levenshulme named after second murder arrest

input.lead: The project forms part of plans to build around 2,000 homes in the wider area
input.summary: The project forms part of plans to build around 2,000 homes in the wider area
input.evidence_text: Oldham housing estate could be built in "beautiful" valley - BBC News Image source, IDPartnership Image caption, The development is a part of plans to build 2,000 homes in the area By Ed Barnes Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 2 hours ago Nearly 200 homes could be built in a "beautiful" valley as part of a major development that includes a new tram stop. Barratt Homes Manchester have asked Oldham Council to approve up to 192 homes at Birshaw Farm in the Beal Valley, Oldham, Greater Manchester. It forms part of wider plans for the area, which includes around 2,000 homes, as well as other infrastructure. There is also a new road planned from Ripponden Road to Oldham Road, as well as a new Metrolink stop at Broadbent Moss. The scheme is part of the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone scheme, which aims to oversee house building, create jobs, and protect the regions's green belt land from unplanned development. The new homes would be built about three miles north of Oldham town centre and includes an area of greenfield land on the edge of Royton. The development will include wetland landscapes, green spaces, as well as accessible walking and cycling routes according to the plans , external . Image source, IDPartnership Image caption, The developers said the project would deliver £36.7m of gross value to the area Despite the loss of farmland to development, a report said the development will keep "existing woodland and mature tree groupings to establish a distinctive landscape character" with an aim to plant 551 new trees. title: Funding boost for historic Wigan Royal Court Theatre

input.lead: Plans to transform the Grade II listed theatre into "a vibrant destination" take a step forward
input.summary: Plans to transform the Grade II listed theatre into "a vibrant destination" take a step forward
input.evidence_text: Plans to bring an historic theatre back into use have taken a major step forward after new investment was approved Wigan's Royal Court Theatre on King Street will receive part of the £3.7m funding Wigan Council is set to receive from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, to support the borough's economy and community developments The Grade II listed theatre, which closed in 1974 and was used as a bingo hall, nightclub and bar, has already received £1.1m in funding for building works Cllr Dane Anderton said the latest funding will help bring the theatre a step closer to becoming "a vibrant destination for residents and visitors" "The Royal Court Theatre is one of Wigan's most recognisable heritage assets and we're delighted to have secured further funding to continue its revival," cabinet portfolio holder for economic development and regeneration at Wigan Council, said "The £1.1 million already invested has helped secure the building's future by carrying out vital protection and restoration works

title: Cheadle mental health wards ordered to improve upgraded to 'good'

input.lead: Cheadle Royal Hospital's child and adolescent mental health wards are now rated good by inspectors
input.summary: Cheadle Royal Hospital's child and adolescent mental health wards are now rated good by inspectors
input.evidence_text: Cheadle mental health wards ordered to improve upgraded to 'good' - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, Inspectors carried out tours of two wards as part of the inspection By Lynette Horsburgh North West Published 1 hour ago Child and adolescent mental health wards at a Greater Manchester hospital that had been ordered to improve has been rated as "good" by health inspectors. The Care Quality Commission (CQC) has upgraded the rating of the service at Cheadle Royal Hospital's child and adolescent mental health wards after an inspection in April. The hospital, run by Affinity Healthcare Limited, provides a range of inpatient mental health services for young people between 11-17 and adults. The inspection followed the receipt of information of concern, the CQC said. CQC inspectors found the hospital had made necessary improvements and was now only in breach of one regulation related to safe care and treatment. At the previous inspection, inspectors found five breaches of regulation. At the time of this latest review, the CQC said there were six young people admitted to the main ward and one young person in long-term segregation on another ward, which was not in general use. Inspectors carried out a tour of the Woodlands and Featherstone wards as well as the clinic room and the ward seclusion suite. The CQC upgraded its rating for how responsive and well-led the service was from "required improvement" to "good", and has again rated how effective and caring the service is as good. The report found: Staff treated young people with compassion and kindness, respected their privacy and dignity and involved them and their families in planning their care Leaders had a good understanding of how the ward was run and were visible and approachable to both staff and young pe

title: Ex Man-Utd player Paul Scholes banned from driving

input.lead: The former Manchester United player banned after speeding twice in two days
input.summary: The former Manchester United player banned after speeding twice in two days
input.evidence_text: Ex Man-Utd player Paul Scholes banned from driving - BBC News Image source, Reuters Image caption, Former Man Utd player Paul Scholes has been for speeding in his Range Rover Published 18 August 2026 Former Manchester United footballer Paul Scholes has been handed a six-month road ban after he racked up two driving convictions in the space of two days. The 51-year-old was caught speeding in a Range Rover on the evening of 3 March while on a late-night drive through Cleckheaton in West Yorkshire. In the second case, Scholes's Mercedes broke the speed limit on Mossley Road near Ashton-under-Lyne, Greater Manchester, on the morning of 14 November last year. On 12 August at Bradford Magistrates' Court, he was handed a six-month driving ban for the first offence, along with fines. The next day at Manchester Magistrates' Court he received six penalty points on his licence, and further fines. Fines, costs, and court fees for the criminal cases totalled £1,472. A court official said Scholes, who was prosecuted in private hearings under the Single Justice Procedure, did not enter pleas to either of the charges he faced and was convicted in his absence. Image source, PA Media Image caption, Scholes was convicted under the Single Justice Procedure Court documents obtained by the Press Association news agency show Scholes's Range Rover was caught speeding at just after 23:30 BST on 3 March on the A649 Halifax Road near Cleckheaton. Police said the former footballer replied to a notice of intended prosecution, confirming he had been the driver. title: Droylsden dad boxes to raise £2k after charity helped his wife

input.lead: Victim Support helped Trish through court proceedings after sexual abuse she suffered as a child
input.summary: Victim Support helped Trish through court proceedings after sexual abuse she suffered as a child
input.evidence_text: Droylsden dad boxes to raise £2k after charity helped his wife - BBC News Image source, Craig Hinde Image caption, Craig says seeing Trish go through the court process made him want to give something back to Victim Support By Haider Saleem North West Published 18 August 2026 A father who had never boxed has raised £2,630 for a charity supporting people affected by crime - after it helped his wife through court proceedings over sexual abuse she suffered as a child. Craig Hinde, 41, from Droylsden, Greater Manchester, trained for eight weeks before taking part in a white-collar boxing event in Manchester. His wife Trish said Victim Support prepared her for court after she reported being sexually abused as a child by her father, Gerard King, who was convicted at Chester Crown Court in 2022. Craig also said it had helped their son Jacob, 10, who took up boxing after being bullied, regain his sparring confidence, showing how trying mattered more than winning. Trish, 38, said she had never been in a courtroom before and described the prospect as "terrifying". The lettings administrator said Victim Support talked her through what to expect and reassured her that it was acceptable to say she did not know or could not remember an answer. "For people who have been through trauma, they often are terrified of not being believed," she said. But she said there was none of that feeling when speaking to the charity. "It's just acceptance and validation," she said. "There's no judgment. They just help you through the process." Image source, Craig Hinde Image caption, Craig said he had avoided physical exercise since injuring his knees at 17 Trish said getting help was "the best thing I ever did" and that she was now a very different person from the one who had gone through the court pro

input.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

Cytix has completed a Series A funding round led by Northern Gritstone, with participation from existing investors Auriga Cyber Ventures and NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance. The latter is managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II. Bosses say the investment will support the rollout of Cytix’s newly launched change risk platform, which monitors software changes and updates to identify and validate potential security risks. They add the technology responds to growing pressure on organisations to keep security controls aligned with increasingly rapid software development, as AI-assisted coding, agentic workflows and continuous delivery accelerate the volume and pace of change.
